purpose.primary: Provide a small formal companion for the Coherence question: Does this hold together?
purpose.formal_goal: Inspect whether a desired conclusion actually follows from the definitions, hypotheses, and relationships supplied in the formal context.
purpose.educational_principle: A plausible conclusion is not enough. The formal structure must support it.

formal_translation: Does the target theorem follow from the formal context actually supplied?

awareness.result: Identify the formal objects, types, hypotheses, and goal.

alignment.result: Identify which declared or proved relationships permit formal correspondence or transformation.

coherence.current_step: Determine whether those pieces and relationships collectively support the target.

coherence_mapping.shared_habit: Inspect whether the pieces work together rather than assuming a conclusion from individually plausible parts.

formal_structure.central_question: Is there a valid formal path from the supplied context to the target?
formal_structure.successful_result: The target is derivable under the represented formal assumptions.
formal_structure.unsuccessful_result: The current proof state remains unresolved and should be inspected before changing the model.

key_distinctions.rule: Formal plausibility does not discharge a proof obligation.
An incomplete proof does not automatically establish that the theorem is false.
Discovering that a theorem requires another assumption does not automatically justify adding that assumption.
A theorem may follow coherently from formal assumptions even when those assumptions have not been empirically validated.
One successful theorem does not establish that every part of the surrounding model is correct.

supported_relationship.definition: A relationship available through definitions, hypotheses, or previously established formal results.
supported_relationship.formal_use: May contribute to deriving the target when the formal rules permit it.
supported_relationship.principle: Make explicit which relationship is doing the work.

missing_relationship.definition: A link required by the desired conclusion but not currently supplied or derivable from the represented formal context.
preferred_response: inspect whether a legitimate theorem can establish it
inspect whether the model omitted something
inspect whether the target is too strong
leave the theorem unproved if the support is absent
missing_relationship.avoid: Invent a premise merely to close the goal.

unsupported_conclusion.principle: A conclusion should not be promoted to a theorem merely because it is desirable or intuitive.
unsupported_conclusion.coherence_question: What exact formal relationship is missing?

contradiction.formal_meaning: The represented assumptions or statements cannot all be maintained consistently under the relevant formal interpretation.
contradiction.principle: Some apparent contradictions arise from mismatched definitions or boundaries rather than genuine logical conflict.

constraint_vs_contradiction.principle: A difficult or unsatisfied proof condition is not automatically a contradiction.

assumptions.principle: Every assumption used to establish the theorem remains part of the result context.
inspection_questions: Is each added assumption justified by the intended model?
Would the theorem still hold without it?
assumptions.warning: A proof can often be made easier by strengthening assumptions, but stronger assumptions may weaken the relationship to the intended source problem.

assumption_ladder.question: Did the formal model improve, or was the target protected by increasingly convenient assumptions?

local_vs_global_coherence.local: An individual definition, theorem, or relationship is formally well-formed or successfully proved.
local_vs_global_coherence.global: The larger collection of definitions, assumptions, relationships, and interpretations works together without hidden incompatibility.
local_vs_global_coherence.principle: Local proof success does not automatically establish global model coherence.

example_pattern: Assume all P objects have property Q.
coherent_but_unsupported.formal_status: The inference may be coherent under the supplied assumptions.
coherent_but_unsupported.empirical_status: The assumptions may still require independent support.
coherent_but_unsupported.principle: Internal validity and empirical support are separate dimensions.

do_not_force_coherence.principle: A formal gap should remain visible when the available structure does not establish the desired relationship.
do_not_force_coherence.avoid: Insert a relationship only because the theorem looks incomplete without it.

repair.principle: Repair should address the identified structural problem rather than merely preserve the original conclusion.

when_not_to_repair.condition: The available formal information is insufficient to determine whether the theorem, model, or missing relationship should change.
when_not_to_repair.principle: An unresolved formal state can be more informative than an unjustified repair.

proof_obligation.role: Make the unresolved formal target visible.
proof_obligation.educational_value: A remaining goal shows exactly what has not yet been established.
proof_obligation.principle: Do not treat an open goal as though it had already been proved.

preferred_process: decide whether the proof, assumption, definition, or target is at fault

formal_success.means: The represented conclusion follows under the supplied formal context and accepted proof.
does_not_mean: the theorem captures the full source interpretation

student_exercise.instruction: Before changing a failed theorem, identify the exact point at which the formal support stops.
student_exercise.purpose: Practice Coherence as diagnosis before repair.

variation_exercises.question: Which theorem or proof step no longer follows?
Does the existing context now support the theorem without additional assumptions?
Did the proof improve, or did the model change?

strengthening_and_weakening.strengthening_question: What new assumptions or lemmas does the stronger claim require?
strengthening_and_weakening.weakening_question: What is the strongest claim the current context actually supports?
strengthening_and_weakening.principle: A narrower supported theorem may be more informative than a stronger theorem obtained only through convenient assumptions.

lean_establishes: whether the represented theorem is accepted under the supplied formal context
lean_does_not_establish: the empirical truth of the assumptions
the relevance of the theorem to every intended real-world case
the coherence of all surrounding informal claims
the correctness of source-to-model mappings not encoded in the theorem
formalization_boundary.principle: Formal Coherence applies first to the explicit model.

source_alignment.guide_concept: Coherence asks whether pieces and relationships work together as a structure.
source_alignment.formal_abstraction: A Lean theorem asks whether a target follows from an explicit formal context.
source_alignment.correspondence: Both expose unsupported relationships, missing assumptions, and structural failure points.
source_alignment.reason: Human-facing Coherence includes informal systems, conflicting goals, evidence, definitions, and empirical relationships broader than theorem proving.

awareness_dependency.principle: A Coherence judgment depends on correctly reading what the formal context actually contains.

alignment_dependency.principle: Coherence depends on mappings and transformations being justified by actual formal relationships.

clarity_bridge.bridge: Once a theorem holds together, the next question is whether its formal structure can be represented clearly enough for another person to inspect.

continuity_connection.question: If assumptions, definitions, or theorem statements change, which coherent proofs survive?
continuity_connection.principle: Coherence can be re-evaluated across formal revisions.

compiler_validation.meaning: The human-source formal artifact was accepted under the stated Lean environment.
compiler_validation.boundary: Compiler acceptance verifies the represented formal artifact under that environment; it does not establish empirical truth or global validity of a source framework.

lean_source_contract.if_embedded: Copy the compiler-checked Lean source exactly rather than reconstructing it from this JSON description.
lean_source_contract.reason: The structured abstraction and the canonical Lean source should not silently diverge.

preferred_support: ask what assumption a theorem requires
identify where the proof state remains unresolved
distinguish a contradiction from a missing relation
explain why a target does not yet follow
suggest a hint without silently changing the theorem
avoid: weakening the target without saying so
changing definitions solely to close the proof
presenting an unresolved theorem as proved

awareness.question: What definitions, hypotheses, and goals are actually present?

alignment.question: Which relationships connect the relevant formal objects?

coherence.question: Do those pieces actually support the target theorem?

clarity.question: Can the proof structure and its assumptions be made visible enough to inspect?

continuity.question: Which parts of the proof survive when the formal model changes?

must: Inspect the supplied formal context before evaluating the target.
Preserve unresolved proof obligations as unresolved.
Identify when a stronger claim requires additional structure.
Distinguish internal formal coherence from empirical validation.
Report compiler validation only at the formal-artifact level.
must_not: invent a missing premise merely to close the theorem
treat proof difficulty as proof of falsity
treat compiler success as empirical validation
silently weaken or change the theorem
claim one proved theorem establishes global model validity
present this artifact as a complete formalization of Coherence
reconstruct Lean source and present it as exact unless verified against the source file

do_not_infer: source code not verified against the formal source file
